text:
oncall-bot: @sanjay paging: detected elevated request queueing across eu-rtx pool >30s median enqueue time for generation calls, error rate 0.4% — please ack and investigate :rotating_light:

sanjay: acked. looking. seeing queue spikes on nodes rtx-eu-02/03. traces show many 1k+ token requests suddenly arriving from a single tenant. not sure if it's traffic surge or a buggy client. digging into request samples now.

eli: heads-up, we have a customer on a dedicated plan running long-context chat, might be related. Eli -> I'll DM them.

sanjay: quick plan: 1) throttle long requests at the edge for eu region (limit max_tokens=1024) 2) spin a small burst pool of smaller instance types to offload shorter jobs 3) failover routing to us-west for non-regulated customers. applying throttles now.

alex: can you paste the command you used to apply the throttle? want to mirror for apac if needed.

sanjay:
```
# edge rate limit config
redwoodctl routes update --region eu --route gen --rate-limit "per-client:5rps,max_tokens:1024"
redwoodctl pool allocate --pool burst-eu-small --instances 4 --gpu-type a10
```

sanjay: applied throttle and added 4 small instances. queue depth dropped ~60% after ~90s. p95 latency improved but p99 still elevated (~4s). overall error rate down to 0.12%.

statusbot: Incident created: INC-2026-0453 "eu inference queueing" — severity: high. Postmortem owner: TBC.

maya: nice mitigation. I'm taking on-call at 21:00 UTC; can you start a handoff summary so I can continue monitoring?

sanjay: +1 handoff in 15m. summary: root cause unknown (spike from a single tenant id: T-8423 & a sudden batch of 1k+ token requests). mitigations applied: edge throttle (max_tokens=1024), burst pool + small instances, routing policy updated to prefer us-west for non-EU tenants. short-term ETA: p99 should be <2s in ~15-20 min if no new spikes. longer-term next steps: traffic shaping for long requests, tenant rate-limiting opt-outs, follow-up with CS for tenant behavior.

maya: thanks. I'll keep an eye. can we put a short status page update and a customer-facing note for affected EU tenants?

sanjay: drafting status update below — please edit: 

--- STATUS PAGE DRAFT ---
Summary: We are investigating increased request queue times affecting inference in our EU region. Some requests are experiencing increased latency and short failures. We have applied throttles to extremely long generation requests and added burst capacity.
Impact: Customers routing through eu region may see higher latency for high-token-generation requests and occasional 5xxs. Most non-EU customers unaffected due to routing fallback.
Mitigation: Edge throttles (max_tokens=1024) and extra small-instance capacity added. We are continuing to monitor and will rollback throttles when p99 returns to normal.
ETA: Monitoring; expected improvement within 30 minutes if no new large request surge.
Contact: status@redwood-inference.com for questions.
--- end ---

maya: tweak: add "We are proactively reaching out to known large-token users." Also add an ETA range 15-45m.

sanjay: updated.

support: draft customer message for EU tenants: 

--- CUSTOMER NOTIFICATION (EMAIL) DRAFT ---
Subject: Incident affecting inference latency in EU region — temporary mitigation applied
Hi <Customer name>,
We detected elevated request queueing impacting inference latency for some workloads in the EU region earlier today. We have applied temporary throttles for extremely long generation requests and provisioned additional capacity to reduce queuing.
What you may see: increased latency for very long generations (>1k tokens) or intermittent errors.
What we did: edge throttles, added burst instances, and routed non-EU traffic to alternate regions where possible.
Next steps: We are investigating the root cause and will follow up if your tenant is identified as the source of the surge. If you require uninterrupted long-context runs, we can coordinate a dedicated path or schedule maintenance with you.
Thanks for your patience — we will update you within 60 minutes or when there is a status change.
Regards,
Redwood Support
--- end ---

maya: good. can we add an explicit opt-out instruction for customers who must run long jobs? like contact support to request a temporary exception or dedicated capacity.

sanjay: added line.

eli: I contacted the tenant T-8423; their engineering says they rolled out a background job that accidentally re-queued large historical exports. they're rolling back now. looks like root cause is client-side.

maya: great find. change of plan: continue monitoring 30m, remove edge throttle for affected customers when they confirm rollback; leave burst pool for now.

sanjay: stepping down to handoff. notes for next oncall (maya): watch queue depth on rtx-eu-02/03, p99 target <2s, escalation if error rate >0.5% or queue depth >200. postmortem owner: ops-lead.

maya: taking over. I'll keep this thread as my watch channel.

statusbot: Status page updated: https://status.redwood-inference.com/incident/INC-2026-0453 — message: "Elevated queueing in EU region; mitigations applied."
